verdict.rationale: Snowflake documents a consumption-based pricing model in which virtual warehouses consume credits that users control directly, plus tiered editions. A community trial user turned credits and storage into a dollar figure and noted that credits double with each warehouse size, which shows rough estimation is possible. However, the pack has no first-party per-credit or storage price tables and no pre-commit cost calculator, and community reports warn that costs can balloon. Missing for 10: documented per-credit and per-TB dollar rates by edition/region, a first-party credits-per-warehouse-size table, a pricing calculator or estimation guide, and corroboration that pre-purchase estimates match actual bills.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, the pricing model is documented clearly enough that I can estimate a monthly bill for my workload before committing

citations.quote: We keep pricing simple with a consumption-based pricing model.

Virtual warehouses consume credits as they execute queries, load data and perform other DML operations. Virtual Warehouses are user-managed, which means you can directly control credit consumption of these resources.
Standard: An entry-level, introductory offering providing access to core functionality.
I have used 9 credits and 40GB of storage... about $19.60 worth of resources.
